context:
Build foundation-first: extract pure helpers (w1) before generating
fixtures (w2), because the fixture generator must mirror the exact
signatures the helpers expose.

Reuse the project's existing Python visualization functions where they
exist as pure helpers - `core/visualization/ascii/heatmap.py` and
siblings delegate to `textcharts`, but the pre-textcharts color/sort
math may live in `result_plotter.py`. If a Python equivalent does not
exist, ADD it (in Python) rather than picking a TS-only number, so
parity is bidirectional.

Fixture format mirrors the textcharts test pattern (if any) so future
contributors recognize the convention. Keep fixtures small and readable
- explicit `id` on each case is mandatory so failures are debuggable.
description:
The 2026-04-15 visualization review identified that the Python CLI
(`benchbox/core/visualization/`) and the Preact explorer
(`results-explorer/src/components/`) reimplement the same
visualization math in two languages with **zero shared computation
and zero contract tests**.

Concrete drift surfaces today:
  - Heatmap color: `colorForCell` (QueryHeatmap.tsx:39-45) duplicates
    `textcharts.heatmap` log10-ratio→hue logic.
  - Per-baseline speedup: `NormalizedSpeedupChart.tsx:57` duplicates
    `textcharts.normalized_speedup` (`baseline / this`).
  - Diverging delta: `DivergingBarChart.tsx:49` duplicates the
    `textcharts.diverging_bar` `(this - baseline) / baseline * 100`
    formula, plus an independent magnitude sort at line 63-67.
  - Per-query "fastest" highlight: Compare.tsx:388-411 inlines its own
    ranking that has no CLI counterpart and disagrees with Compare's
    summary-card definition (see explorer-unify-visualization-foundations
    for the dual-definition bug).

The user requirement is explicit: **"there should be only ONE place
where visualization values are composed, when that is not possible
we must have test infrastructure that ENSURES the parallel
implementations match."** This item builds that test infrastructure.
Centralizing computation server-side is tracked separately
(explorer-emit-comparison-artifact-from-pipeline).

Strategy: Python emits canonical fixtures (input data + expected
output values) for every chart-type computation. Vitest loads the
fixtures and asserts that the explorer's pure helper functions produce
byte-identical numbers (within float tolerance). Any future drift
fails CI, regardless of which side changes.

anti_patterns.dont: commit auto-regenerated fixtures without inspecting the diff
anti_patterns.instead: `make parity-check` must be run separately to detect diffs
anti_patterns.why: the fixture IS the contract and silent regeneration hides drift

anti_patterns.dont: generate fixtures from the TS side
anti_patterns.instead: Python (the canonical compute layer) emits, TS verifies
anti_patterns.why: that makes Python the follower, not the source of truth

anti_patterns.dont: inline the math back into components after extraction

anti_patterns.instead: every helper must have at least one null-input case
anti_patterns.why: that is exactly where Python and JS often disagree (NaN vs null)

anti_patterns.dont: use `toEqual` for floats in the parity suite
anti_patterns.why: IEEE-754 noise differs between Python and JS

work_units.notes:
Move the math out of the SVG components into pure functions:
  - `colorForCell`, `lightnessForCell` (already pure, re-export from QueryHeatmap)
  - `speedupRatio(baselineMs, thisMs)` from NormalizedSpeedupChart.tsx:57
  - `deltaPct(thisMs, baselineMs)` from DivergingBarChart.tsx:49
  - `sortByMagnitudeDesc(entries)` from DivergingBarChart.tsx:63-67
  - `perQuerySpeedup(timings)` (slowest/fastest) from Compare.tsx:388-393
  - `geomeanMs(samples)` (median-based reduction matching transformer)
Components import these helpers; no behavior change. Each helper
returns plain numbers - no SVG, no DOM - so Vitest can call them
directly from a fixture loop.
work_units.summary: Audit and extract pure computation functions out of every explorer chart component into testable helpers in `results-explorer/src/lib/chartMath.ts`

work_units.notes:
Pytest-runnable script (or a regular pytest test using
`--generate-fixtures` flag) that produces files at
`tests/parity/fixtures/{chart_name}.json` with shape:

  {
    "chart": "heatmap_color",
    "version": 1,
    "cases": [
      {"id": "fastest_in_col", "input": {"ms": 100, "minInCol": 100},
       "expected": {"hue": 120}},
      {"id": "ten_x_slower",   "input": {"ms": 1000, "minInCol": 100},
       "expected": {"hue": 0}},
      ...
    ]
  }

One fixture file per chart computation listed in w1. Cases must
include: identity (ratio=1), boundary (ratio=10 clamp), missing
data (None/null), and at least one realistic mid-range value.

Fixtures are CHECKED INTO GIT - they are the contract. Regenerating
them must be a deliberate act (changes the contract) and require
the Vitest suite to accept the new numbers via re-run.
work_units.summary: Build Python fixture generator at `tests/parity/generate_visualization_fixtures.py` that emits JSON fixtures per chart computation

work_units.notes:
Pattern: read each `tests/parity/fixtures/*.json` (relative path
computed in vitest config), iterate `cases`, call the corresponding
TS helper from `chartMath.ts`, assert
`Math.abs(result - expected) < 1e-9` for floats and strict equality
for ints/strings.

Use `describe.each` or generator pattern so each case appears as
its own test name (debuggable on failure). On a fixture mismatch,
the failure message must show: chart name, case id, input, expected
vs actual, and the suspected source of drift (Python file vs TS file).
work_units.summary: Add Vitest parity suite at `results-explorer/src/__tests__/parity/chartMath.parity.test.ts` that loads each fixture and asserts equivalence

work_units.notes:
- `make parity-fixtures` regenerates fixtures via the Python script
- `make parity-check` runs Python generation into a tmpdir, diffs
  against the checked-in fixtures, fails if they differ
- GitHub Actions: run `make parity-check` AND `cd results-explorer
  && npm test` on every PR
- Document the workflow in `docs/contributing-to-explorer.md`
  (or new `docs/visualization-parity.md`): "If you change a chart
  computation, regenerate fixtures with `make parity-fixtures` -
  this changes the contract; reviewers must approve the diff."
